summary: Dieter George worked in Indology and held a post at the Berlin State Library from around 1972 to 1985, succeeding Wolfgang Voigt.

Specializing in Indology, Buddhist studies, and history and archaeology, Dieter Schlingloff worked at the German Academy of Sciences at Berlin (~1954–1962), the University of Kiel (~1968–1972), and Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich as Professor (~1972–1996) and Honorary Professor (~1996).

Tibetologist Dieter Schuh studied under Shri Krishna Sharma and at the University of Cologne (~1965–1967). He served as a special professor in Tibetology at the University of Bonn (~1978–2007) and founded the International Institute for Tibetan and Buddhist Studies.

Dietmar Rothermund was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Marburg (~1953–1954), Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1954–1956), and the University of Pennsylvania (PhD, ~1956–1959). He held a post at Heidelberg University (attested 2004).

Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Shechen Gyaltsap Gyurme Pema Namgyal (~1925–1926), Dzongsar Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Khenpo Shenga, and taught numerous prominent figures including the 14th Dalai Lama.

Dilip K. Chakrabarti, an expert in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at the University of Calcutta (~1959–1965). He worked at Calcutta (~1965–1977), the University of Delhi (~1977–1990), and as Professor of South Asian Archaeology at Cambridge (~1990–2008).

Dilip Kumar Roy is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts in the Department of Museology at the University of Calcutta, where he was attested as Reader in 1982 and attested in 1994.
Dilli Raman Regmi was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned an M.A. from Patna University (~1937–1944) and an M.Litt from the University of Madras.
Dina Bangdel worked in history, archaeology, and religious studies. She held posts at Ohio State University (attested 2006) and Virginia Commonwealth University (~2007–2017).

Specialist in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics Dines Andersen studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1879–1892) under Vilhelm Thomsen, Michael Viggo Fausbøll, and Karl Verner. He later served as professor of Indian philology at Copenhagen (1903–1927).

Indologist and historian Dineschandra Sircar was Lecturer (1937) and Carmichael Professor (1962) at the University of Calcutta. He also served as Government Epigraphist for India with the Archaeological Survey of India (until 1961, attested 1963) and the Government of India.

Ding-hwa Evelyn Hsieh, a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, completed her PhD at the University of California, Los Angeles. In 1998, she was appointed professor of Philosophy and Religion at Truman State University.
Dipak Kumar Barua is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as a Dean at the University of Calcutta in 1987 and was head of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara from around 1996 to 2002.

Dipak Ranjan Das, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, studied under Dineschandra Sircar and was affiliated with the Department of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta (attested 1994).

Historian Dipesh Chakrabarty studied at Andrew's High School, University of Calcutta (~1966–1969), IIM Calcutta (~1969–1971), and Australian National University (~1977–1980). He taught at the University of Melbourne (~1985–1995) and joined the University of Chicago in 1995.

Dirk H. A. Kolff is an Indologist and historian who earned his MA at Leiden University (~1960–1967). He served at Leiden University as Professor of Modern Indian History in 1967 and held a post there from 1991 to 2003.

Indologist and philosopher Diwakar Acharya studied under Ramananda Giri and earned a PhD at the University of Hamburg (~2000–2004). He held posts at Nepal Sanskrit University, Kyoto University, Hamburg, and Oxford (~2016, succeeding Alexis Sanderson).
Dixian was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Mingzu. He served as the abbot of Guanzong Temple from around 1912 to 1932.

Indologist Dominic Goodall studied under Alexis Sanderson (earning a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford by 1995) and Srinivasa Ayya Srinivasan. He served at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (2000) and École Pratique des Hautes Études (2005).

Dominic Sur, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, studied at Harvard and the University of Virginia under Khenpo Lama Chönam, David Germano, Karen C. Lang, and Kurtis R. Schaeffer. He held a post at Utah State University (attested 2017).
